title: Fog
description: herb's night photograph of Times Square, with fog that knows how far away everything is. Drag up or scroll to roll it in, down to clear it; it gathers thickest wherever the pointer rests, like breath on the glass. The far screens go first, dissolving into fields of their own colour, the street haze builds, and herb and the pedicab stay dark and sharp in front of it all. Every sign wears a soft coloured halo as wide as the fog in front of it is deep, and the air itself takes on the neon.
intent: After Michael Kenna's fog photographs (https://www.michaelkenna.com/), Todd Hido's foggy night streets in Excerpts from Silver Meadows (https://www.toddhido.com/), and the depth-true fog of Blade Runner 2049's night city, kept photographic. Beer-Lambert transmittance per pixel through a metric distance converted from a Depth Anything V2 map of herb's own photo, with in-scattered city light and depth-gated neon halos from a weighted bloom pyramid.
